changes: at or below the art. 155 ceiling for that employee, apply that figure directly, unchanged period to period -- do NOT recompute the one-fifth-of-the-excess-over-SMMLV formula each payroll run against a fixed court-specified amount. Art. 155 CST binds the issuing judge, not only the employer (Constitutional Court T-891 of 2013; Funcion Publica Concepto 251611 de 2022: "los jueces solo pueden embargar ... en una quinta parte"), so a validly issued order is presumed to already respect that limit. The one-time check against the cap (the prior point) is what a NEW order needs on receipt; a standing, court-fixed monthly amount does not need re-testing against the fluctuating SMMLV-plus-one-fifth formula every period. Statutory benefits (prestaciones sociales) are not garnishable in any amount. The only exceptions are maintenance (alimentos) and cooperative debts, and even then the garnishment may not exceed 50% of the benefit concerned (CST art. 344). A salary garnishment for any other debt therefore does not reach the statutory service bonus, severance savings or the interest on them.

heading: Example 5 — Complex scenario: all-inclusive salary above the exemption threshold
context: The 13-minimum-wage floor and the 70%-then-ceiling sequence, extended. Labour Code art. 132 num. 2 (as substituted by Law 50 de 1990 art. 18) sets the minimum all-inclusive salary at 10 minimum wages of ordinary salary PLUS a factor of not less than 30% of that amount -- 13 minimum wages in total, C
changes: The 13-minimum-wage floor and the 70%-then-ceiling sequence, extended. Labour Code art. 132 num. 2 (as substituted by Law 50 de 1990 art. 18) sets the minimum all-inclusive salary at 10 minimum wages of ordinary salary PLUS a factor of not less than 30% of that amount -- 13 minimum wages in total, COP 22,761,765 for 2026 (confirmed in UGPP's own published guidance, "ABC Trabajadores dependientes que devengan salario integral"). Fall below 13 minimum wages and the clause is void: the payment reverts to an ordinary salary in full, with statutory benefits owed on top, not absorbed. The worked example above never tests the 25-minimum-wage ceiling because 70% of COP 25,000,000 (17,500,000) sits well below it. The sequence matters, so it is worth making explicit with a number that actually binds: for the SAME executive on an all-inclusive salary of COP 70,000,000, 70% is 49,000,000 -- ABOVE the 25-minimum-wage ceiling of 43,772,625. The 70% factor is applied FIRST, to the full all-inclusive salary; the ceiling is then tested against THAT result, not against some pre-adjusted figure -- so the contribution and payroll-levy base for this employee is capped at 43,772,625, not at 70% of some ceiling-adjusted salary. Confirmed in the same UGPP guidance ("Tope Maximo 25 SMMLV... El IBC no debe superar este tope") and in Consejo de Estado / Ambito Juridico commentary that the 25-minimum-wage ceiling is unaffected by how the underlying pay was structured. The withholding-tax and vacation-accrual treatment do not change: both still run on the full COP 70,000,000, exactly as in steps 4 to 6 above, since the ceiling is a social-security-contribution rule only. CONFIRMED AGAIN 19 September 2026, directly from the statute's own sequence: Ley 100 de 1993 art. 18, as rewritten by Ley 797 de 2003 art. 5, states the rules in this order within the SAME article -- (i) the base is the monthly salary, (ii) "el limite de la base de cotizacion sera de 25 salarios minimos", THEN, as the article's next and final substantive rule, (iii) "las cotizaciones de los trabajadores cuya remuneracion se pacte bajo la modalidad de salario integral, se calculara sobre el 70% de dicho salario." Rule (iii) computes what "la base de cotizacion" IS for an integral-salary worker; that resulting figure is then the thing tested against the ceiling already stated in rule (ii) -- the statute never gives a separate, pre-adjusted ceiling for salario integral. This is not merely UGPP's reading; it follows from the order the amending article itself uses.

changes: Usually structured as non-salary under a written art. 128 pact, so it stays out of the IBC up to the limit of Ley 1393 de 2010 art. 30: non-salary payments above 40% of the month's total remuneration enter the IBC at the ordinary flat rates. If taxable, it is simply added to the month's other labour income for the ordinary art. 383/388 depuration; the 95-tax-unit figure some client processes cite is the ceiling of the FIRST bracket of the general art. 383 table (0% rate up to 95 tax units), which applies to all labour-income depuration -- it is not a bonus-specific rule and does not gate whether social security applies (HRBS-12487 confirmed this misconception, 18 September 2026).

changes: STRONGER WARNING for any automated build of this wage type (HRBS-12487, 18 September 2026): the client-side automation spec reviewed for this ticket applies an 8%/9%/10% bracket structure DIRECTLY TO THE BONUS AMOUNT before computing withholding (e.g. 9% x a bonus of 12,940,200 = 1,164,618 treated as 'SS'). This does not correspond to any real Colombian social-security mechanism -- contributions are a FLAT percentage of the employee's MONTHLY IBC (8% baseline, +1% FSP only when that month's TOTAL IBC reaches 4 SMMLV), never a graduated bracket applied to one isolated payment, and this bonus, when paid non-salary, stays out of the IBC except for any part of the month's non-salary payments above the 40% limit of Ley 1393 de 2010 art. 30. Built as specified, the engine would withhold social security not owed, THEN compute income-tax withholding on a base already wrongly reduced by that deduction -- one defect compounding into a second. The art. 383 progressive-table mechanics in the same spec (bracket boundaries, 28% rate, 10 UVT fixed value) ARE correctly transcribed; the error is entirely upstream, in treating the bonus as social-security-contributable at all. Build with NO social-security deduction on this wage type; add the bonus to the month's other labour income for ordinary depuration only.

Given there is no bonus-specific social-security deduction on this wage type (only the part of the month's non-salary payments above the Ley 1393 de 2010 art. 30 40% limit, if any, enters the IBC at the ordinary flat rates), the build is simpler than the spec frames it -- 62837 stays at the GROSS bonus, with one deduction line for withholding tax only, computed under ordinary art. 383/388 depuration. The spec correctly excludes WT 62838 (becas/scholarships) from any deduction regardless of amount -- that exclusion is right and should be preserved unchanged.
